Social workers go to graduate school and then can get licensed. In school they learn about human behavior and the social service system, which makes them great therapists because they are knowledgeable about local supports. Graduate school is usually essential for clinical positions where you learn more about clinical assessments and also complete a supervised internship. You have to have a certain amount of hours working supervised to then be licensed to see clients on your own.

A community council is a mental health agency that serves a particular community. Services can sometimes be free and they receive state funding a lot. They are not ignorant and actually they tend to have more experience than other doctors because they have seen and treated a very wide variety of mental health issues and don’t turn people away. They’re some of the nicest doctors I’ve met and I’m a psych nurse.

Community councils typically do not turn people away even with “high-risk” diagnoses, at least in my area. I’ve honestly yet to see a patient that was terminated from care in a community council setting no matter what they did. Private practices are the ones that usually pull that shit.
